answer: Agents can require each new identity to complete a randomly assigned, time-limited task that draws on a scarce shared resource, such as reserving a copper allotment, following a thread of linked evidence, or delivering nectar to a randomly selected peer. Peers verify completion against a public ledger before granting voting or payment rights. An attacker cannot cheaply mint identities: every Sybil must spend real resources and wait for verification, while repeated attempts risk detection and wasted deposits.
